title: ConfigProvider
description: Provides the theme and the language of lib-core to your application, and exposes them through useConfig().

usage.title: Usage
usage.text: Render one ConfigProvider at the root of your application. It applies the theme as CSS variables on <html>, sets the language of lib-core's built-in texts, and provides both to useConfig().
usage.dynamic: Both props are reactive: store them in state to let users switch theme or language at runtime.
usage.global: Theme and language are global: the provider writes CSS variables on <html> and changes lib-core's i18next language. A nested ConfigProvider therefore re-themes the whole page, not only its children. To theme a single region, set the CSS variables on a wrapper element instead (see the custom theme example).

palette.title: Palette, persistence and callbacks
palette.text: palette adds a color palette ("editorial", "tech", "graphite" or "cool") on top of the light, dark or system theme. persist saves theme and palette changes in the theme and palette cookies and restores them after hydration. onThemeChange and onPaletteChange are called after setTheme and setPalette change the value.
palette.setters: useConfig() also returns mode, resolvedMode and palette, and the setTheme and setPalette setters, so any component can switch the theme without lifting state. Server rendering, cookies and the no-flash init script are covered in

use-config.title: Reading the configuration
use-config.description: useConfig() returns the configured theme, the resolved theme and the locale of the nearest provider. Change the site theme in the header to see it update.

custom-theme.title: Custom theme
custom-theme.description: A custom theme built from themes.light. Passed to ConfigProvider it would re-theme the page; here its tokens are applied as CSS variables on one container.

locale.title: Locale
locale.description: The locale prop sets the language of lib-core's built-in texts (en, zh or fr). The demo restores English when it unmounts, because the language is global.

palette.title: Palettes
palette.description: The four palettes previewed side by side in the site's current mode, with data-palette and data-theme on each card. With the palette prop the same attributes go on <html>.

ConfigContextProviderProps.theme: Theme to apply: "auto" or its alias "system" (follows prefers-color-scheme), a built-in theme name, a theme object, or a { light, dark } pair. Applied as CSS variables on the document root, or through a palette when palette is set.
ConfigContextProviderProps.palette: Palette applied with the light, dark and system themes ("editorial", "tech", "graphite", "cool"); null keeps Minerva's default look. Sets data-palette on <html>; the palette tokens come from style.css.
ConfigContextProviderProps.persist: Persist theme and palette changes in the theme and palette cookies and restore them after hydration (pair it with THEME_INIT_SCRIPT for SSR).
ConfigContextProviderProps.onThemeChange: Called after setTheme changes the theme.
ConfigContextProviderProps.onPaletteChange: Called after setPalette changes the palette.
ConfigContextProviderProps.locale: Language of lib-core's built-in texts (changes it globally).

ConfigContextProps.theme: Theme as configured (may be "auto" or a { light, dark } pair).
ConfigContextProps.resolvedTheme: Theme currently applied after resolving "auto" and { light, dark } pairs: a built-in theme name or a theme object.
ConfigContextProps.locale: Current locale of lib-core's built-in texts.
ConfigContextProps.mode: Color mode of the theme: "light" or "dark" for those themes, "system" for "auto", "system" and { light, dark } pairs, undefined for other themes.
ConfigContextProps.resolvedMode: Applied color mode (data-theme on <html>), when it can be determined.
ConfigContextProps.palette: Active palette (data-palette on <html>), null for Minerva's default look.
ConfigContextProps.setTheme: Changes the theme (saved to the theme cookie when persist is on).
ConfigContextProps.setPalette: Changes the palette (saved to the palette cookie when persist is on).

Locale.language: Language of lib-core's built-in texts: "en", "zh" or "fr".

context.title: ConfigContext
context.text: useConfig() throws when there is no ConfigProvider above it, which catches setup mistakes early. Read ConfigContext directly when the provider is optional: it returns undefined instead of throwing.
